body.p: Applicant replies to the Office Action dated April 25, 2024 within three months. Claims 1, 3, 6-10, 14, and 16-20 are pending in the application, and the Examiner rejects claims 1, 3 and 6- 10, and claims 14 and 16-20 were not address in the Office Action. Since claims 14 and 16-20

were not address in the prior Office Action, Applicant requests that if another Office Action is issued, that the Office Action be a non-final office action. Support for the amendments may be found in the originally-filed specification, claims, and figures. No new matter is entered with these amendments. Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration of this application.

Applicant thanks the Examiners for their time conducting the Examiner Interview that took place on July 25, 2024 with Applicant's Representative. Applicant and the Examiners agreed in the Examiner Interview that the proposed amendments overcome the outstanding rejections, but further search and consideration would be required. Accordingly, Applicant asserts that the rejections should be withdrawn and the claims as amended are in condition for allowance.

The Office rejects claims 1, 8 and 9 under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b) or 35 U.S.C. 112 (pre-AIA), second paragraph, as being indefinite for failing to particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter which the inventor or a joint inventor, or for pre-AIA the Applicant, regards as the invention. Applicant respectfully disagrees with these rejections, but Applicant presents claim amendments in order to clarify the patentable aspects of the claims and to expedite prosecution.

The Office rejects claims 1, 3 and 6-9 under 35 U.S.C. § 102(a)(1) as being anticipated by Ta, US Publication No. 2019/0192039 ("Ta"). Applicant respectfully disagrees with these rejections, but Applicant presents claim amendments in order to clarify the patentable aspects of the claims and to expedite prosecution. Applicant and the Examiners agreed in the Examiner Interview that the proposed amendments to claim 1 overcame the 102 rejection. Accordingly, Applicant asserts the rejection should be withdrawn and claim 1 is in condition for allowance.

The Office rejects claim 3 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Ta as applied to claim 1 above, and further in view of Ben-Haim, US Publication No. 2020/0286225 ("Ben- Haim"). The Examiner rejects claim 10 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Ta as applied to claim 8 above, and further in view of Krebs, US Publication No. 2019/0205766 ("Krebs"). Applicant respectfully disagrees with these rejections, but Applicant presents claim amendments in order to clarify the patentable aspects of the claims and to expedite prosecution. Applicant incorporates dependent claim 3 into independent claim 1. Applicant and the Examiner agreed in the Examiner Interview that the amendments overcome the outstanding rejections. Accordingly, Applicant asserts that the rejection should be withdrawn and the claims are in condition for allowance.

In view of the above remarks, Applicant respectfully requests withdrawal of all rejections. The Examiner is invited to telephone the undersigned at the Examiner's convenience, if that would help further prosecution of the subject application. The Commissioner is authorized to charge any fees due, or any deficiency in the fee(s) filed or asserted to be filed, or which have been filed herewith or concerning any paper filed hereafter and which may be required under 35 C.F.R. §§ 1.16 - 1.18 (deficiency only) now or hereafter relative to this application and the resulting official document under 37 C.F.R. § 1.20 or credit any overpayments to Deposit Account No. 19-2814. This statement does not authorize to charge the issue fee.
